set_title: Crypto- and cocci- names: Cryptococcus, Cryptosporidium, Coccidioides, Cyclospora
stem: A 28-year-old man from Phoenix has 3 weeks of cough, fever, joint pain and tender red nodules on the shins. Chest x-ray shows hilar adenopathy. Sputum KOH preparation shows thick-walled spherules containing endospores.
oneliner: 28-year-old man, Arizona, cough, erythema nodosum, spherules with endospores → ?

whyNot.A: Shows encapsulated yeasts in CSF; his sputum shows **spherules with endospores**
whyNot.B: Causes diarrhea after imported produce; he has **cough and erythema nodosum**
whyNot.D: Shows tiny yeasts in macrophages in Ohio valley; he has **spherules in Arizona**
whyNot.E: Shows broad-based budding yeasts in the Great Lakes; he has **spherules with endospores**

why: Cocci- (berry) + -oides: berry-like spherules. **Desert Southwest, erythema nodosum and spherules with endospores** indicate valley fever.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Great Lakes; broad-based buds; lung plus skin**

idea.rule: Spherules with endospores in the Southwest = Coccidioides; yeast in macrophages = Histoplasma.
also: Valley fever; endemic in Arizona and California

set_title: Crypto- and cocci- names: Cryptococcus, Cryptosporidium, Coccidioides, Cyclospora
stem: A 40-year-old man who explored a bat-inhabited cave in Kentucky has 2 weeks of fever, dry cough and weight loss. Chest x-ray shows hilar adenopathy. Biopsy shows oval yeasts 2-4 micrometers inside macrophages.
oneliner: 40-year-old man, caving in Kentucky, tiny oval yeasts inside macrophages → ?

whyNot.B: Shows large encapsulated yeasts with halos; his yeasts are **tiny and inside macrophages**
whyNot.C: Causes watery diarrhea; he has **cough, hilar adenopathy and intracellular yeasts**
whyNot.D: Shows spherules in the Southwest; he has **yeasts in macrophages after a Kentucky cave**
whyNot.E: Shows broad-based budding yeasts with skin lesions; his yeasts are **small and intracellular**

why: Histo- (tissue) + plasma (formed body): first mistaken for a tissue protozoan. **Cave and bat exposure with tiny yeasts inside macrophages** indicate it.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Great Lakes; broad-based buds; lung plus skin**

idea.rule: Tiny yeast inside macrophages + bats and caves = Histoplasma.

set_title: Ka- names: Kawasaki, Kaposi, Kasabach-Merritt, Kartagener, Kallmann
stem: A 24-year-old man has chronic sinusitis, recurrent bronchitis and infertility with normal sperm count but immotile sperm. Chest x-ray shows dextrocardia and CT shows bronchial dilation.
oneliner: 24-year-old man, infertile with immotile sperm, sinusitis, heart on the right → ?

whyNot.A: Causes fever and vasculitis in children; he has **sinusitis and dextrocardia**
whyNot.B: A vascular tumor in HIV; he has **sinusitis, dextrocardia and immotile sperm**
whyNot.C: Causes thrombocytopenia in a vascular tumor; he has **sinusitis and dextrocardia**
whyNot.E: Causes anosmia and absent puberty; he has **immotile sperm and dextrocardia**

why: Kartagener: dynein arm defect makes cilia immotile. **Chronic sinusitis, bronchiectasis, dextrocardia and immotile sperm** fit.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: eponym: platelets trapped in vascular tumor
eponym: ciliary dyskinesia with situs inversus
eponym: GnRH neurons fail to migrate

idea.rule: Kartagener = ciliary dynein defect: sinusitis, bronchiectasis, situs inversus, infertility.

set_title: B- bacteria: Bordetella, Borrelia, Bartonella, Brucella, Burkholderia
stem: A 22-year-old man with cystic fibrosis has worsening cough, fever and a rapid decline in FEV1. Sputum grows a glucose-nonfermenting gram-negative rod resistant to aminoglycosides and polymyxins, and he later develops bacteremia.
oneliner: 22-year-old man, cystic fibrosis, declining lungs, resistant nonfermenting rod → ?

whyNot.A: Causes whooping cough in infants; he has **cystic fibrosis and a resistant rod**
whyNot.C: Is spirochetal and tick-borne; he has **a resistant nonfermenting rod in sputum**
whyNot.D: Causes cat-scratch adenitis; he has **cystic fibrosis lung decline**
whyNot.E: Causes undulant fever after livestock exposure; he has **lung decline with a resistant rod**

why: Burkholderia cepacia complex infects the lungs in cystic fibrosis or chronic granulomatous disease. **Rapid FEV1 decline with a resistant nonfermenting rod** fits.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Cat scratch, tender regional nodes; bacillary angiomatosis**
**Undulant fever; goat cheese or farm animals**

idea.rule: CF lung decline with a resistant rod that is not Pseudomonas = Burkholderia cepacia.
also: Also infects chronic granulomatous disease patients

stem: A 62-year-old man with alcohol use disorder has fever and a cough productive of thick, red, mucoid sputum. Chest x-ray shows an upper-lobe consolidation with a bulging fissure and cavitation. Culture grows mucoid, lactose-fermenting gram-negative rods.
oneliner: 62-year-old alcoholic man, currant jelly sputum + upper-lobe consolidation with cavitation + mucoid gram-negative rods → ?

whyNot.A: Streptococcus pneumoniae is a gram-positive diplococcus; his culture grows **gram-negative rods**
whyNot.B: Mycoplasma has no cell wall and no Gram stain; his culture grows **gram-negative rods**
whyNot.D: Chlamydophila causes a mild atypical pneumonia; he has **cavitation with currant jelly sputum**
whyNot.E: Pneumocystis affects the severely immunosuppressed; he has **cavitation and gram-negative rods**

why: Encapsulated, lactose-fermenting gram-negative rod that necroses lung. **An alcoholic with currant jelly sputum and an upper-lobe cavity** is Klebsiella.

idea.rule: Five -pneumoniae bugs: match by host, sputum, and Gram stain.

stem: A 19-year-old college student has had 10 days of low-grade fever and a dry cough, but is well enough to attend class. Chest x-ray looks worse than expected, with patchy interstitial infiltrates. Cold agglutinins are positive, and sputum Gram stain shows no organisms.
oneliner: 19-year-old student, 10 days of dry cough, still in class + patchy infiltrates + cold agglutinins + no organisms on Gram stain → ?

whyNot.A: Streptococcus pneumoniae causes lobar rusty-sputum disease; he has **patchy infiltrates, no organisms**
whyNot.C: Klebsiella causes cavitary pneumonia in alcoholics; he has a **mild dry cough**
whyNot.D: Chlamydophila can look similar but does not produce **cold agglutinins**
whyNot.E: Pneumocystis needs severe immunosuppression; he is a **healthy student**

why: Smallest free-living bacterium, no cell wall, so no Gram stain and no response to beta-lactams. **Walking pneumonia with cold agglutinins** is Mycoplasma.

idea.rule: Mycoplasma: no cell wall, cold agglutinins, macrolide or doxycycline.

stem: A 35-year-old man with HIV, a CD4 count of 90/mm3, and no prophylaxis has 3 weeks of dry cough and breathlessness on exertion. LDH is high. Chest x-ray shows bilateral diffuse ground-glass opacities. Silver stain of lavage fluid shows cysts.
oneliner: 35-year-old man, HIV CD4 90 + dry cough and exertional dyspnea + ground-glass opacities + silver-stain cysts → ?

whyNot.A: Streptococcus pneumoniae causes lobar consolidation; he has **bilateral ground-glass opacities with a low CD4**
whyNot.B: Klebsiella causes cavitary lobar pneumonia; he has **bilateral ground-glass opacities**
whyNot.C: Mycoplasma infects healthy young people; he has **CD4 of 90 and silver-stained cysts**
whyNot.E: Chlamydophila causes mild illness in normal hosts; he has **CD4 of 90, hypoxemia**

why: Yeast-like fungus, opportunistic when CD4 falls below 200. **Dry cough, ground-glass opacities and silver-stain cysts in AIDS**; treat with TMP-SMX.

idea.rule: Pneumocystis jirovecii: fungus, CD4 under 200; TMP-SMX treats and prevents.

stem: A 60-year-old woman who had a splenectomy 5 years ago has sudden fever, shaking chills and a cough with rust-colored sputum. Chest x-ray shows right lower lobe consolidation. Sputum shows lancet-shaped gram-positive diplococci that are sensitive to optochin.
oneliner: 60-year-old woman, asplenic + sudden fever, rusty sputum + lobar consolidation + lancet gram-positive diplococci → ?

whyNot.A: Klebsiella is a gram-negative rod; her sputum shows **gram-positive diplococci**
whyNot.B: Mycoplasma has gradual onset and no cell wall; she has **sudden fever, lancet diplococci**
whyNot.C: Mycobacterium tuberculosis gives subacute cough and acid-fast bacilli; she has **sudden fever, diplococci**
whyNot.E: Pneumocystis causes diffuse ground-glass disease in AIDS; she has **lobar consolidation and diplococci**

why: Encapsulated gram-positive diplococcus; asplenia removes capsule clearance. **Rusty sputum, lobar consolidation and lancet diplococci that are optochin-sensitive**.

idea.rule: Strep pneumoniae: lobar, rusty sputum, optochin-sensitive, bile-soluble.

set_title: Broncho- names: bronchiolitis, bronchiolitis obliterans, bronchopulmonary dysplasia and their look-alikes
stem: A 4-month-old boy, born at term, has had a runny nose for 3 days and now has a cough, fast breathing and poor feeding. It is January, and his older sister has a cold. He has nasal flaring, intercostal retractions, and wheezes and fine crackles over both lungs.
oneliner: 4-month-old boy, term, winter + 3 days of runny nose, then cough, retractions, wheeze and crackles → ?

whyNot.B: Bronchiolitis obliterans is chronic fixed scarring; he has a **3-day illness after a cold**
whyNot.C: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia follows preterm ventilation; he was **born at term**
whyNot.D: Bronchiectasis means years of purulent sputum; his illness is **3 days old**
whyNot.E: Bronchogenic cyst is a mediastinal mass; he has **wheeze and crackles over both lungs**

why: Small airway + inflammation: an acute viral infection, mostly RSV. **An infant's winter cold that moves down to wheeze and retractions** is bronchiolitis.

head: Means
One clue
rows: **Infant's winter cold moving down to wheeze**
**Preterm, ventilated, still on oxygen at 36 weeks**
**Daily purulent sputum; airway wider than artery**

idea.rule: Bronchiolitis = acute viral in infants; obliterans = chronic scar. Same root, opposite course.
also: Supportive care; RSV antibodies prevent it

set_title: Broncho- names: bronchiolitis, bronchiolitis obliterans, bronchopulmonary dysplasia and their look-alikes
stem: A 3-month-old boy was born at 26 weeks' gestation and needed surfactant, mechanical ventilation and supplemental oxygen for 8 weeks. He still needs oxygen through a nasal cannula, breathes fast, and gains weight slowly. A chest x-ray shows coarse streaky opacities mixed with overinflated areas in both lungs. He has had no fever.
oneliner: 3-month-old boy born at 26 weeks + 8 weeks of ventilation and oxygen + still oxygen-dependent, streaky lungs → ?

whyNot.A: Bronchiolitis obliterans scars airways, usually after transplant; he was **born at 26 weeks, ventilated**
whyNot.B: Bronchiolitis is a viral cold-like illness; he has **needed oxygen since birth, no fever**
whyNot.C: Bronchopulmonary sequestration is one systemic-artery segment; he has **changes in both lungs**
whyNot.D: Bronchiectasis means years of purulent sputum; he is **3 months old, oxygen since birth**

why: Airway + lung + abnormal growth: the lung did not grow normally. **Very preterm, ventilated, still on oxygen weeks later** is bronchopulmonary dysplasia.

head: Means
One clue
rows: **Infant's winter cold moving down to wheeze**
**Preterm, ventilated, still on oxygen at 36 weeks**
**Daily purulent sputum; airway wider than artery**

idea.rule: Preterm + ventilator + oxygen, still needing oxygen at 36 weeks = bronchopulmonary dysplasia.
also: Oxygen and pressure halt alveolar growth
Sequestration shares the name; it is a malformation

set_title: Broncho- names: bronchiolitis, bronchiolitis obliterans, bronchopulmonary dysplasia and their look-alikes
stem: A 47-year-old woman has had a daily cough for 3 years that brings up large amounts of thick, foul-smelling yellow sputum, sometimes streaked with blood. She had a severe pneumonia at age 30. She has clubbing and coarse crackles at both lung bases. CT shows thick-walled airways in both lower lobes that are wider than the arteries beside them.
oneliner: 47F + 3 years of daily cough with copious purulent sputum + clubbing + airways wider than arteries in both lower lobes → ?

whyNot.A: Bronchogenic cyst is one carinal mass; she has **widened airways in both lower lobes**
whyNot.B: Bronchiolitis obliterans gives a dry cough; she has **copious purulent sputum and dilated airways**
whyNot.C: Bronchopulmonary sequestration is one disconnected segment; she has **dilated airways in both lower lobes**
whyNot.E: Bronchiolitis is a viral illness of infants; she is **47 with a 3-year cough**

why: Airways + widening: the bronchi are permanently dilated. **Years of purulent sputum, clubbing, and airways wider than their arteries** is bronchiectasis.

head: Means
One clue
rows: **Infant's winter cold moving down to wheeze**
**Preterm, ventilated, still on oxygen at 36 weeks**
**Daily purulent sputum; airway wider than artery**

idea.rule: Bronchiectasis = dilated airways full of pus; obliterans = closed airways, dry cough.
also: Causes: cystic fibrosis, ciliary dyskinesia, ABPA, old pneumonia
CT: signet ring sign and tram tracks
